tasks.title: Lecture #8
tasks.instruction: Listen to a speaker talking to a class on a trip to a marine aquarium.
tasks.transcript:
Now you will hear a speaker talking to a class on a trip to a marine aquarium.
Hello, everyone. Thank you for visiting the aquarium today. I hope you’ve enjoyed seeing the thousands of fish we have here, as well as the other sea animals. During the next hour we’re going to show you some more sea creatures. They all come from a body of water called the Sargasso Sea. The Sargasso Sea is actually part of the Atlantic Ocean. What I mean is---it isn’t a separate body of water; it’s more like a sea within an ocean. It’s located off the southern half of North America, and it is very large----it covers millions of kilometers. Now, a couple of things make it distinctive. First, and probably most important, the waters there are very calm—calm and warm. There’s also very little wind there. Surrounding the Sargasso Sea are water currents in the Atlantic that move in a circular motion, counterclockwise. This water swirls around the Sargasso Sea. Because of the way these currents move, the water in the middle of the Sargasso Sea doesn’t move much at all. Because of the still waters and the lack of wind, sailing ships crossing the Atlantic travel much more slowly when they get to the Sargasso Sea. Without wind, sailboats can get stuck there for long periods. Something else that’s unusual about the Sargasso Sea is the seaweed floatingon its surface. Large amounts of a kind of seaweed called sargassum float on top of the water there.
And because of the currents, the seaweed stays in the Sargasso Sea, it’s kind of held in place by the rotating currents.
Now this seaweed is what interests us most here at the aquarium, because it supports all kinds of sea life, like shrimp, crabs, and fish. Sargassum creates an ecosystem for them to live in. What makes this ecosystem quite remarkable is that the creatures there are one you’d expect to find much closer to shore, much closer to land, not out in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean. Most likely, sargassum probably did not exist in the Sargasso originally. Rather, the seaweed and some of the ecosystem it supported drifted out into the Sargasso Sea long ago and became trapped there by the currents. From there, it simply spread all over the Sargasso Sea.

questions.stem: What is the speaker mainly talking about?

options.A: An unusual part of the Atlantic Ocean
options.B: A kind of seaweed that is eaten by most fish
options.C: The discovery of an uncommon type of seaweed
options.D: A kind of sea animal that lives only in the Atlantic Ocean

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：演讲者主要在谈论什么？ 定位原文：They all come from a body of water called the Sargasso Sea. The Sargasso Sea is actually part of the Atlantic Ocean. What I mean is it isn't a separate body of water; it's more like a sea within an ocean. 选项分析： A. An unusual part of the Atlantic Ocean（大西洋中一个不同寻常的区域）。由于演讲者整体介绍了马尾藻海的位置、洋流特征、平静的水面以及独特的生态系统，这些都是在描述大西洋中一个不寻常的区域，因此A选项正确。 B. A kind of seaweed that is eaten by most fish（一种被大多数鱼类食用的海藻）。因为演讲中没有提到海藻被大多数鱼类吃掉，而是说海藻为海洋生物提供栖息环境，所以B选项错误。 C. The discovery of an uncommon type of seaweed（一种不常见海藻的发现）。基于演讲者没有讨论海藻的发现过程，所以C选项错误。 D. A kind of sea animal that lives only in the Atlantic Ocean（一种只生活在大西洋中的海洋动物）。由于演讲重点不在某种特定动物上，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what do certain currents in the Atlantic Ocean do?

options.A: They cause the Sargasso Sea to become smaller and smaller over time
options.B: They keep the water in the middle of the Sargasso Sea from moving much
options.C: They make fish from the Sargasso Sea drift to other place
options.D: They prevent seaweed in the Sargasso Sea from being eaten by sea creatures

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：根据演讲者，大西洋中的某些洋流做了什么？ 定位原文：Surrounding the Sargasso Sea are water currents in the Atlantic that move in a circular motion, counterclockwise. This water swirls around the Sargasso Sea. Because of the way these currents move, the water in the middle of the Sargasso Sea doesn't move much at all. 选项分析： A. They cause the Sargasso Sea to become smaller and smaller over time（它们导致马尾藻海随时间推移越来越小）。因为没有提到洋流使马尾藻海缩小，所以A选项错误。 B. They keep the water in the middle of the Sargasso Sea from moving much（它们使马尾藻海中部的水几乎不流动）。由于洋流以逆时针方向环绕马尾藻海旋转，导致中间的水几乎不动，因此B选项正确。 C. They make fish from the Sargasso Sea drift to other place（它们使马尾藻海的鱼类漂到其他地方）。基于演讲中没有提到洋流使鱼类漂走，所以C选项错误。 D. They prevent seaweed in the Sargasso Sea from being eaten by sea creatures（它们防止马尾藻海的海藻被海洋生物吃掉）。因为洋流的作用与防止海藻被吃无关，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What is the speaker explaining when he mentions sailing ships?

options.A: How the Sargasso Sea was discovered
options.B: How seaweed got into the Sargasso Sea
options.C: How unusual the water in the Sargasso Sea looks
options.D: How little wind there is in the Sargasso Sea

questions.analysis: 答案：D 题目问的是：演讲者提到帆船时是在解释什么？ 定位原文：Because of the still waters and the lack of wind, sailing ships crossing the Atlantic travel much more slowly when they get to the Sargasso Sea. Without wind, sailboats can get stuck there for long periods. 选项分析： A. How the Sargasso Sea was discovered（马尾藻海是如何被发现的）。由于帆船的例子与发现过程无关，所以A选项错误。 B. How seaweed got into the Sargasso Sea（海藻是如何进入马尾藻海的）。因为帆船的讨论与海藻来源无关，所以B选项错误。 C. How unusual the water in the Sargasso Sea looks（马尾藻海的水看起来多么不寻常）。基于演讲者没有用水的外观来解释帆船的问题，所以C选项错误。 D. How little wind there is in the Sargasso Sea（马尾藻海的风多么少）。由于演讲者明确指出因为缺乏风，帆船经过马尾藻海时速度会大幅减慢，甚至被困很长时间，这正是用帆船的例子来说明该区域风力极小，因此D选项正确。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what is surprising about some animal species that live in the Sargasso Sea?

options.C: They are usually found closer to land
options.D: They are not native to the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：根据演讲者，生活在马尾藻海的某些动物物种令人惊讶之处是什么？ 定位原文：What makes this ecosystem quite remarkable is that the creatures there are one, you'd expect to find much closer to shore, much closer to land, not out in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean. 选项分析： A. They have short life spans（它们寿命很短）。因为没有提到这些动物寿命短，所以A选项错误。 B. They are larger than expected（它们比预期的更大）。由于演讲中没有提到动物体型大小，所以B选项错误。 C. They are usually found closer to land（它们通常被发现在更靠近陆地的地方）。基于演讲者强调令人惊讶的是这些生物通常应该在靠近海岸的地方被发现，而不是在大西洋中央，因此C选项正确。 D. They are not native to the Atlantic Ocean.（它们不是大西洋的原生物种）。因为演讲者没有说这些动物不是大西洋原生的，所以D选项错误。
